newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends up but still in range.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends up but still in range.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures, helped by reports of a firmer weekend cash, ended up slightly Friday in sluggish trade, but prices remained in recent technical ranges, industry sources said.
July firmed 1.1 cents to close at $2.188 per million British thermal units. August settled 1.5 cents higher at $2.198. Most other months ended up by 0.4 to 1.4 cents.

"We held minor (July) support at $2.16, then shorts covered ahead of the close, but I think we could see pressure next week. There's no longer-term weather support and we should see more rolling of length from the front," said one trader.

While temperatures early next week, may warm up slightly in the Northeast, most of the rest of the nation is expected to range from normal to slightly-below normal, dimming chances for much improvement in air conditioning demand.

Traders said there was little or no impact from a small, natural gas line leak in the Vermilion Bay area offshore Louisiana. Several lines were shut last night for testing, but major pipeline operators said Friday flows were normal.

Technical traders said the market was still range-bound, with July resistance seen at $2.25, and then at $2.37 and the contract high of $2.44. Support was pegged at $2.10, with stronger buying expected at $2.08.

In the weekend cash, Gulf Coast prices firmed slightly Friday to the mid-teens. Midcon pipes were two to three cents higher at about $2.05. New York city gate gas prices were up slightly to about $2.40.
The NYMEX 12-month Henry Hub strip rose by 1.3 cents to $2.256. NYMEX said 24,473 contracts traded, down from Thursday's revised tally of 29,164.

On the KCBT, July finished 1.5 cents lower at $2.035, while deferreds ended narrowly mixed. The East/West spread widened by 2.6 cents to 15.3 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 149 lots traded, down from Thursday's total of 432.
